newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin due back in office on Monday-spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin due back in office on Monday-spokesman.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will return to Moscow from his country residence at the weekend and will begin work in his Kremlin office on Monday after his November 5 heart surgery, his press secretary said on Friday.

Itar-Tass news agency said that Yeltsin was planning to make his first televised address to the nation since the operation later on Friday. "This is completely possible," a duty officer in the presidential press office said.
Yeltsin has spent more than two weeks in the Rus residence some 100 km (65 miles) west of Moscow.
Press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing that Yeltsin's plans for his first days back at work included meetings with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and senior Kremlin aides.
He said doctors had advised the 65-year-old president to take things easy and not to overwork.
Yeltsin has given some brief television interviews since his bypass heart operation but has not resumed his traditional radio and television addresses.
